# NRC Public Dose Limits — 10 CFR Part 20, Subpart D

## 1. Direct answer

| # | Limit | Dose quantity | Value (regulatory units) | Value (SI) | Citation |
|---|-------|---------------|--------------------------|------------|----------|
| 1 | Annual limit to an individual member of the public from the licensee's operations | Total effective dose equivalent (TEDE) = external deep-dose equivalent + committed effective dose equivalent from intakes | **0.1 rem in a year** (= 100 mrem/yr) | **1 mSv in a year** (= 1000 µSv/yr) | 10 CFR 20.1301(a)(1) |
| 2 | Limit in any unrestricted area, any one hour | Dose from **external sources** only, in the unrestricted area (no internal component) | **0.002 rem in any one hour** (= 2 mrem/h) | **0.02 mSv (20 µSv) in any one hour** | 10 CFR 20.1301(a)(2) |

The governing provision is **10 CFR Part 20, Subpart D, § 20.1301, "Dose limits for individual members of the public"** (current eCFR text). Both limits are mandatory: §20.1301(a) states "Each licensee shall conduct operations so that—" both (a)(1) and (a)(2) are satisfied simultaneously.

## 2. Regulatory text (verified quotation)

> "§ 20.1301 Dose limits for individual members of the public.
> (a) Each licensee shall conduct operations so that—
> (1) The total effective dose equivalent to individual members of the public from the licensed operation does not exceed 0.1 rem (1 mSv) in a year, exclusive of the dose contributions from background radiation, from any medical administration the individual has received, from exposure to individuals administered radioactive material and released under § 35.75, from voluntary participation in medical research programs, and from the licensee's disposal of radioactive material into sanitary sewerage in accordance with § 20.2003, and
> (2) The dose in any unrestricted area from external sources, exclusive of the dose contributions from patients administered radioactive material and released in accordance with § 35.75, does not exceed 0.002 rem (0.02 millisievert) in any one hour."
> — eCFR, 10 CFR 20.1301 (fetched 2026-11-15, sha256 2b39065f96c2)

## 3. How to apply each limit

**Annual limit — §20.1301(a)(1)**
- Applies to the **maximally exposed individual member of the public** receiving dose from the licensed operation; it is not a population-average or collective-dose limit.
- Quantity is **TEDE**: sum of deep-dose equivalent (external) and committed effective dose equivalent (internal, from inhalation/ingestion of effluent). Both pathways count.
- **Excluded** from the 0.1 rem: natural background; medical administration to the individual; dose from patients released under §35.75 (and, per (a)(2), such patients' contribution is also excluded from the hourly limit); voluntary participation in medical research; and licensee sewage disposal under §20.2003.
- Compliance is normally demonstrated per §20.1302 by measurement or calculation for the individual likely to receive the highest dose (e.g., boundary dose modeling, environmental monitoring, or effluent concentration limits in Appendix B, Table 2).

**One-hour limit — §20.1301(a)(2)**
- Applies to the **unrestricted area** — an area to which access is neither limited nor controlled by the licensee for radiation protection purposes (so the boundary fence line, site perimeter, and any publicly accessible location are the operative points).
- Quantity is **external-source dose only**; internal dose from effluents is not part of this test. It is evaluated as the maximum dose in **any** one hour (a clock-hour/instantaneous peak), not an average.
- Compliance is normally demonstrated by boundary dose-rate surveys or calculational dose-rate estimates (typically with instruments reading in mrem/h or µSv/h).
- Practical note: an instrument reading of **2 mrem/h (20 µSv/h)** at the unrestricted-area boundary saturates this limit exactly; anything above it is a violation regardless of the annual total.

## 4. Unit conversions (both directions)

| Quantity | rem / mrem | sievert |
|---|---|---|
| Annual public limit | 0.1 rem = 100 mrem | 1 mSv = 1000 µSv |
| Hourly unrestricted-area limit | 0.002 rem = 2 mrem | 0.02 mSv = 20 µSv |

Conversion used: 1 rem = 10 mSv; 1 mrem = 10 µSv.

## 5. Relationship between the two limits — do not conflate them

These are independent constraints, and the one-hour limit is **not** an annual allowance divided by 8760 hours. Worked check (this is the consistency test for the numbers above):

- Annual limit expressed as an average rate: 0.1 rem/yr ÷ 8760 h/yr = **1.14 × 10⁻⁵ rem/h = 0.0114 mrem/h ≈ 0.114 µSv/h**.
- Hourly cap: **0.002 rem/h = 2 mrem/h ≈ 20 µSv/h**.
- Ratio: 2 mrem/h ÷ 0.0114 mrem/h ≈ **175×**. Sustained at the hourly cap for a full year the dose would be 0.002 × 8760 = **17.52 rem/yr**, i.e., 175 times the annual limit. Therefore the annual limit is the binding constraint on cumulative exposure; the hourly limit exists to prevent short-term spikes/hot spots in areas the public can occupy.
- Sanity check the other way: at 2 mrem/h, a member of the public would accumulate the full 100 mrem annual limit in **50 hours** of occupancy. That is why licensees control occupancy duration as well as dose rate at the boundary.

Stating either figure as if it were the other (e.g., quoting "2 mrem per hour" as an annual limit, or "100 mrem per year" as the hourly limit) is the most common error in this area.

## 6. Related figures that are NOT the answer (avoid quoting these by mistake)

- **Occupational limit:** 5 rem (50 mSv) TEDE per year, 10 CFR 20.1201(a)(1). Applies to adult workers, not members of the public.
- **Alternative-compliance external-dose criteria (practitioner note — confirm against §20.1302 text, which was not in the verified quotation set):** under §20.1302(b)(2), a licensee may demonstrate compliance by showing effluent concentrations at the unrestricted-area boundary do not exceed Appendix B Table 2 and that, if an individual were continuously present in an unrestricted area, the external-source dose would not exceed **0.002 rem (0.02 mSv) in an hour and 0.05 rem (0.5 mSv) in a year**. The 0.05 rem/yr external-only figure is a component of the alternative demonstration; it does not replace the 0.1 rem/yr TEDE limit of §20.1301(a)(1).
- **EPA limit, uranium fuel cycle:** 40 CFR 190 sets 25 mrem/yr whole-body to the public for the nuclear fuel cycle; it is implemented through NRC licenses and can be the more restrictive number for fuel-cycle facilities. It is an EPA standard, not the Part 20 public dose limit.

## 7. Interpretation points and caveats

- **"Member of the public"** — per 10 CFR 20.1003, any individual except when receiving an occupational dose. Workers, and individuals administered radioactive material, are outside this class for the purposes of these limits.
- **Members of the public inside a controlled area** — §20.1301 continues to apply to such individuals (i.e., allowing public access to a controlled area does not switch them to occupational limits); confirm the exact wording of the remaining paragraphs of §20.1301 against the current eCFR before relying on it in a licensing document.
- **Jurisdiction** — these are NRC licensee requirements. Agreement States adopt compatible regulations (generally Part 20 verbatim), but a State may have a more restrictive rule; verify the State rule for a State-licensed facility.
- **Version** — the values above reflect the current eCFR text of §20.1301.
